ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let [m]_q = (1−q^m)/(1−q), let (a;q)_k = ∏_{j=0}^{k−1} (1−aq^j), let (a,b,c;q)_k = (a;q)_k (b;q)_k (c;q)_k, and let Φ_n(q) be the nth cyclotomic polynomial. Prove that for positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r)=1 and r ≤ d, and for every integer n > 1 with n ≡ 1 mod 2d, we have Σ_{k=0}^{n−1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^(k(d−dk−2r)/2) / (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k ≡ [rn]_q q^(r(1−n)/2) mod [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2.

k is a nonnegative integer in the notation definitions and a summation index from 0 to n minus 1 in the theorem.
d and r are positive integers.
gcd(d, r) = 1.

n is congruent to 1 modulo 2d.
The modulus is the product of the q-integer [n]_q and the square of the nth cyclotomic polynomial Phi_n(q).

Prove that for positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r)=1 and r ≤ d, and for every integer n > 1 with n ≡ 1 mod 2d, we have Σ_{k=0}^{n−1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^(k(d−dk−2r)/2) / (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k ≡ [rn]_q q^(r(1−n)/2) mod [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2.

payload.proof_nl: Let R = Q[q,q^{-1}] and let S = {V(q) in Q[q] : gcd(V(q), M(q)) = 1}. By definition, Loc_M = S^{-1}R. Since R is an integral domain and every element of S is nonzero, the canonical map S^{-1}R -> Frac(R) is injective; and Frac(R) = Q(q). So we may regard Loc_M as a subring of Q(q). Now gcd(U(q), M(q)) = 1, so U(q) belongs to S. Therefore U(q) is invertible in Loc_M, and because H(q) is in R, the element H(q)/U(q) belongs to Loc_M. The hypothesis gives the identity U(q)(X(q)-Y(q)) = M(q)H(q) in Q(q). Since U(q) is a nonzero rational function, we may divide by U(q) in Q(q) and obtain X(q)-Y(q) = M(q)·(H(q)/U(q)). The factor H(q)/U(q) lies in Loc_M, so the right-hand side belongs to M(q)·Loc_M. Hence X(q)-Y(q) belongs to M(q)·Loc_M. By the definition of congruence modulo M(q), this is exactly X(q) ≡ Y(q) mod M(q).
payload.role_in_assembly: Provides the correct localization-compatible final cancellation step for rational functions.

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For any nonzero coprime polynomials M and U over the rationals, if X and Y are elements of the M-localized Laurent polynomial ring and their difference becomes divisible by M after multiplying by U, with the quotient represented by some Laurent polynomial H, then X and Y are congruent modulo M in that localization.
quantifier_order: For all nonzero polynomials M and U in q over the rationals, with gcd of U and M equal to 1
Define Loc_M as the localization of the Laurent polynomial ring in q over the rationals obtained by inverting every polynomial coprime to M
For all X and Y in Loc_M
If there exists H in the Laurent polynomial ring in q over the rationals such that U times the difference X minus Y equals M times H in the rational function field in q
Then X is congruent to Y modulo M, meaning X minus Y lies in the ideal generated by M inside Loc_M

payload.statement_nl: Let M(q) and U(q) be nonzero elements of Q[q] with gcd(U(q),M(q))=1. Let Loc_M be the localization of the Laurent polynomial ring Q[q,q^{-1}] obtained by inverting every polynomial V(q) in Q[q] with gcd(V(q),M(q))=1. For rational functions X(q) and Y(q) in Q(q), write X(q) ≡ Y(q) mod M(q) if X(q)-Y(q) belongs to the ideal M(q)·Loc_M. Assume X(q) and Y(q) both belong to Loc_M. If there exists H(q) in Q[q,q^{-1}] such that U(q)(X(q)-Y(q))=M(q)H(q) in Q(q), then X(q) ≡ Y(q) mod M(q).

dependency_assessment.notes: No external citations were used. The proof relies only on the lemma’s definitions and standard algebraic facts about localization of a domain and its embedding into the fraction field.

detailed_findings.finding: The proof is complete and uses the correct localization-cancellation argument intended by the lemma sketch.

result_payload.reason: The proof correctly identifies the localization as a subring of the rational function field, uses gcd(U,M)=1 to show U is invertible in the localization, rewrites the given identity as X-Y = M·(H/U), and observes H/U ∈ Loc_M. This directly proves X-Y ∈ M·Loc_M, which is exactly the stated congruence. The argument matches the lemma sketch and the intended assembly role.
